messages.subject: hdfs.read.text.file in to R
parts:
I am trying to using hdfs.read.text.file to read data from HDFS in to
R.

The data is importing into a list of strings. When I try to use
strsplit I end up getting a list of lists. Here is my sample code.

diag <- c()

filepath <- "/user/root/county1"
x <- hdfslist.files(filepath)
dirlen <- nchar(filepath) + 2

x.df <- data.frame(x)

for (i in 1:nrow(x.df))
{
filename <- x.df[i, 6]

if (substring(filename, dirlen, dirlen + 8) != "_SUCCESS" &&
substring(filename, dirlen, dirlen + 5) != "_logs")
{
tmp <- hdfs.read.text.file(filename)

diag <- append(diag, tmp)
print (filename)
}
}

messages.subject: Re: hdfs.read.text.file in to R
parts:
if your file contains comma separated values, you could use read.table with textConnection to create a data frame.

x  <- "first,second,third,fourth" 
x1 <- read.table(textConnection(x), sep = ",")

However, this is really not an rhdfs issue, it is R programming question.  I suggest to post this to the R-devel mailing list to solicit input from others on the optimum way of converting the text to a dataframe.

messages.subject: Re: hdfs.read.text.file in to R
parts:
A couple more thoughts on this matter

1.  You could use a pipe to feed directly into "read.table".  In this case the "pipe" is a connection object used by read.table

out<-read.table(pipe("hadoop dfs -cat '/tmp/testdata/test.csv'"), sep=",", header=TRUE) 

2.  You could also use  HttpFS (http://archive.cloudera.com/cdh4/cdh/4/hadoop/hadoop-hdfs-httpfs/) or WebHDFS (http://hortonworks.com/blog/webhdfs-%E2%80%93-http-rest-access-to-hdfs/) to specify a URL as a "connection" object in R
